originalTitle: Ghanaians' ICC petition over migrant attacks 'opportunistic', says South Africa
title: Being Kind to Everyone: News from Africa!
content:
Hello from Your Friendly African Reporter!

Hello, amazing kids! It's me, your friendly news reporter, bringing you exciting and important stories from our wonderful continent, Africa! Today, we're talking about something very important: being kind to everyone, no matter where they come from.

What is Happening?

Imagine you live in a beautiful country, like Ghana. And imagine some people from Ghana move to another beautiful country, like South Africa, to live or work. Most of the time, this is a happy thing! People meet new friends and learn new things. But sometimes, things can get a little tricky. Recently, some people from Ghana were worried about people from other countries who are living in South Africa. They were worried that some people were not being treated kindly. So, they decided to ask a very important court for help. This court is called the International Criminal Court, or ICC for short.

Who are Migrants?

A 'migrant' is just a special word for someone who moves from one country to live in another. Think of it like moving to a new school or a new town. People move for many reasons! Maybe their parents got a new job, or they want to be closer to family, or they are looking for a safer place to live. When people move, they bring their stories, their yummy food, and their happy songs! They add so much to their new home. Did you know? People have been moving and traveling all over Africa for thousands of years! It's how different cultures have met and shared wonderful things!

Where is This Happening?

Our story today takes us to two amazing African countries. First, there's Ghana, a country in West Africa with beautiful beaches and rich history. Then there's South Africa, a big country at the very bottom of Africa, famous for its wild animals like lions and elephants, and its tall mountains. Both Ghana and South Africa are part of our big African family. It's like brothers and sisters in a big family, sometimes they need to talk things through.

What is the ICC (The Special Court)?

The ICC, or International Criminal Court, is like a super, super important judge for the whole world! It's not for small problems, but for very, very serious problems that happen to many, many people. It's like when a big bully hurts lots of kids, and a very strong grown-up steps in to make sure it stops and everyone is safe. The ICC's job is to make sure that people are safe and treated fairly everywhere. It listens to very big problems and tries to help find a fair solution. Did you know? The ICC is in a country called the Netherlands, very far away from Africa! But its decisions can help people all over the world, including in Africa.

Why Did Ghana Ask for Help?

The people from Ghana were very worried. They said that some people from other countries living in South Africa were getting hurt. They felt it was a very, very serious problem, like 'crimes against humanity'. 'Crimes against humanity' sounds like a big, scary phrase, right? It means when really, really bad things happen to many, many people, just because of who they are or where they come from. It's when a lot of people are hurt over and over again. The people from Ghana thought this was happening and wanted the big world court to look into it. They wanted to make sure that everyone, no matter where they are from, is safe and treated with respect in South Africa.

How Did South Africa Feel?

South Africa heard about Ghana's request to the big world court. South Africa said, "Wait a minute! We are a strong country, and we can solve our own problems." They felt that Ghana should have talked to them first, or that going to the big world court was not the best way to fix things right now. South Africa wants to make sure everyone is safe too. They believe they can protect everyone living in their country and make sure they are treated fairly. They were not happy that Ghana went straight to the super court.

Why is Being Kind Important?

This story reminds us all how important it is to be kind to everyone. Imagine if you moved to a new place. You would want new friends to welcome you, right? Everyone deserves to feel safe and happy, no matter if they are from a different town, a different city, or a different country. When people from different places live together, they can share so much! New foods, new music, new ways of doing things. It makes our communities stronger and more colourful. Did you know? Many countries in Africa have people living there from all sorts of different places, bringing their own special traditions and stories!

What Happens Next?

The world is watching to see how South Africa makes sure that everyone living in their country is safe and treated fairly. It's a big job for a country to look after all its people, plus all the people who have come to live there from other places. It's important that countries talk to each other and work together like good neighbours and good family members. Our big African family wants to see everyone living in peace and harmony. So, remember, kids: be kind, be welcoming, and always treat others how you want to be treated! That's the best news of all!
summary: People from Ghana are worried about how people from other countries are being treated in South Africa, so they asked a special world court for help, but South Africa said they can fix their own problems.
whyMatters: This is important because everyone, no matter where they come from, deserves to be safe and treated kindly, and countries should work together to make sure that happens for everyone.

originalTitle: Even camels can't cope: Africa's ships of the desert hit by rising temperatures
title: Africa's Camels Are Feeling the Heat!
content:
Hello, amazing friends! It's your kid-friendly news reporter, here to tell you something very important happening in beautiful Africa. We have so many wonderful animals here, and today we're going to talk about a very special one: the camel!

Meet the Mighty Camels!

Camels are amazing animals. They are super strong and have long legs. They live in very hot places called deserts, where there is a lot of sand and not much water. People often call camels "ships of the desert." Can you guess why? It's because they can walk across the vast, sandy deserts for many, many days. They carry people and heavy things, just like ships carry things across the ocean! Did you know? Camels can close their nostrils to keep sand out during a sandstorm! How cool is that?

What's Inside a Hump?

Many people think a camel's hump is full of water. But guess what? It's not! A camel's hump is actually full of fat. This fat gives them energy when there's no food. When a camel uses up all its fat, its hump gets floppy! But don't worry, it fills up again when they eat well. This fat also helps them stay cool in the hot sun. Did you know? A camel can drink up to 40 gallons of water in just a few minutes! That's like filling up almost 200 big soda bottles!

Africa is Getting Hotter!

Our beautiful home, Africa, is known for its sunny weather. But lately, something new is happening. The sun is getting hotter and hotter. It’s like someone turned up the heat on a giant oven! This very, very hot weather is called "extreme heat." It means the days are super warm, and sometimes even the nights don't cool down much. This can be hard for everyone, even for our tough camels.

Camels Are Feeling Sick!

Normally, camels are champions at living in the heat. They have thick fur to keep the sun off them, and they can go a long time without water. But now, even they are finding it too much. Herders are special people who look after camels. They are like farmers, but for camels! These herders are seeing their camels get very tired and sick. The camels don't want to walk or eat. They just want to rest and find shade. Did you know? Camels have extra thick lips so they can eat thorny desert plants without hurting themselves!

Why Are Camels So Important?

Camels are not just pretty animals; they are super important to many families in Africa. They give milk, which is a very healthy drink for children and grown-ups. They also help people carry things to market or bring water from faraway wells. Without healthy camels, life becomes much harder for these families. The herders worry a lot when their camels are not well.

What Are Experts Saying?

Smart people called "experts" are studying this problem. They are scientists who look at the weather and animals. They say that the world is getting warmer, and this is making places like Africa even hotter. They call this "rising temperatures." It means the heat is not just a little bit more, but it’s going up and up over the years. This extra heat is what is making our camels suffer. Did you know? Baby camels are called calves, just like baby cows! They are super cute!

What Happens When It's Too Hot?

Imagine playing outside on a super hot day. You get tired, thirsty, and maybe a little grumpy, right? That's how our camels are feeling. When it's too hot for too long, camels can get dehydrated. That means they don't have enough water in their bodies, even if they drank a lot earlier. They can also get heatstroke, which is very dangerous and makes them very sick.

Why Does This Matter to Us?

When animals like camels suffer, it’s a big problem. It tells us that our world is changing. We need to take care of our planet so that all living things, including us, can be happy and healthy. Helping our camels also means helping the people who depend on them. We want everyone in Africa to have happy families and strong animals. Did you know? There are two main types of camels: Dromedary camels, which have one hump and live in Africa and the Middle East, and Bactrian camels, which have two humps and live in colder parts of Asia!

What Can We Do?

Even though we are kids, we can still help! We can learn more about our amazing planet and how to keep it healthy. We can try to save electricity by turning off lights when we leave a room. We can save water by turning off the tap when we brush our teeth. These small things can make a big difference together! Let’s talk to our families and friends about how important it is to keep our Earth cool. We want our camels to be happy and strong again, carrying their important loads and giving their yummy milk. Thank you for listening, my wonderful friends! Let’s all do our part to help Africa's camels and our amazing planet!
summary: Africa's amazing camels, usually super good at living in hot places, are now getting sick because the weather is becoming too, too hot.
whyMatters: This matters because healthy camels help many families in Africa, and their sickness tells us our planet is getting too warm, which is bad for everyone and everything.
